items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
items.summary_1line: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning. items.editor_note: Names the cost of always-on steering and proposes gating it per token.

items.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
items.summary_1line: Proposes TASK memory, which pairs a text note with activation steering and a removable knowledge edit to reduce use-time memory hallucinations in frozen LLMs, reporting memory-ignoring errors cut to at most 1.5% across ten model-dataset cells.
items.editor_note: First application to agent memory, with a reported error ceiling of 1.5% across ten model-dataset cells.

editorial.tldr: A Nov 13 paper argued that SAE steering applied to every token pushes representations off-distribution and proposed per-token gating that follows the generation trajectory. A Nov 19 paper then recast RL post-training of diffusion transformers as activation steering, tying a costly training step to an inference-time intervention.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 25 paper, TASK memory, pairs each text memory note with activation steering and a removable knowledge edit, reporting memory-ignoring errors cut to at most 1.5% across ten model-dataset cells on frozen LLMs.
editorial.why_it_matters: Activation steering is moving from a behavior knob into agent memory, so teams fighting memory hallucination on open-weight models get a no-fine-tuning option beyond better retrieval and prompting.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agent ignores or misuses its stored notes on a frozen open-weight model, add a memory-ignoring error rate to your evals now so you can compare TASK-style steering against your current retrieval setup.

open_questions: How much generation quality does trajectory-aware gating recover compared with steering every token?
Can a steering vector reproduce the RL post-training gains in diffusion transformers without running RL?
What latency and storage cost does TASK memory add per stored memory compared with text-only notes?
Do TASK memory's removable knowledge edits stay isolated when many memories are active at once?
